title: Give payroll and floor planning the rules they asked for

blocks.text: The warehouse's `Timesheets` class serves two teams. Payroll pays workers from it, and floor planning builds its weekly cover report from it. Both have always started from the same number, `worked(shift)`: time on site less the break.
Two requests arrived for this month's release:

items: **Payroll**, after the new union agreement: each shift is paid in whole quarter hours of time worked. A shift with 8h20 worked is paid for 8h15.
**Floor planning**: a break shorter than 20 minutes is taken at the workstation, so the report counts it as time on the floor. A longer break doesn't count.

blocks.text: Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Timesheets.java`, `Payroll.paidMinutes(...)` and `FloorReport.floorMinutes(...)`, and change anything else in the file you need to. When you're done, each team gets its new rule, and neither team's numbers change because of the other team's request. About four lines in total.

cases.says: shifts worked in whole quarter hours with long breaks are paid and reported as the time worked
each shift is paid in whole quarter hours of time worked, the rest of a quarter hour unpaid
the floor report counts a break shorter than 20 minutes as time on the floor
payroll's quarter-hour rounding does not change the minutes on the floor report
floor planning's short-break rule does not make a break paid

origin.section: Each Actor Owns Its Rules, Even When They Look Identical

concepts: Each actor's class keeps its own rules, even ones that look identical to another actor's, so a change for one actor leaves the other's results as they were.
